basis: Annular erythema of infancy is a dermal disorder; no systemic organ damage is established.
Skeletal dysplasia defined by limb shortening and skeletal abnormalities across both subtypes.
Neoplasm located in the sternum, a skeletal structure.
The named syndrome combines focal alopecia and congenital brain enlargement; no additional organ involvement is documented.
Hirschsprung disease, sensorineural hearing loss and pigmentary abnormalities define this syndrome; iris pigmentation is non-damaging; common neurologic damage is unproven.
Treponema pallidum infection directly inflames and damages the aorta and sometimes the aortic valve.
Congenital skeletal myopathy with weakness in 16/16; respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness rather than intrinsic lung damage.
Hypertrophy of pyloric muscle obstructs the gastric outlet; vomiting and dehydration do not establish another damaged organ.
Infection directly inflames the external ear and ear canal.
Optic nerve degeneration defines OPA12; larger series show hearing loss in 4/22 and neurologic findings below 30%, despite high frequencies in small subsets.
Progressive idiopathic fibrosis directly damages lung parenchyma; reflux is a separate associated disease and clubbing is a sign.
Cortisol excess causes myopathy/bone loss, skin atrophy and endogenous immunodeficiency, each reported at 30-79%; hypertension is separately diagnosed.
The syndrome is defined by structural shoulder-girdle defects and familial intellectual disability; further organ involvement is undocumented.
Craniosynostosis and CNS malformations define the syndrome; optic atrophy directly damages vision in 80-99%.
Bacterial biofilm-mediated dental caries destroys dentine; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Sarcoma occupies the kidney; mesenchymal histology does not establish locomotor-system involvement.
Tumor arises in the exocrine pancreas; possible local invasion does not establish common damage to another organ axis.
Primary immunodeficiency; intellectual disability occurs in 2/5 and motor delay in 2/4. Recurrent otitis is a separate infection without established lasting ear damage.
Marrow hypocellularity 4/4; nail/skin changes and oral leukoplakia 3/4 define dyskeratosis. Cerebellar hypoplasia and developmental delay occur in 4/4.
Meningeal tumor affecting the CNS visual pathway; optic-nerve subtypes exist, but common direct ocular damage across the umbrella is not established.
GH deficiency/metabolic disease; cataracts and deafness 4/4, sensory neuropathy 3/3. Cap omits skeletal dysplasia/scoliosis (3/3) and achalasia (80-99%).
Inherited aneurysmal disease directly affects the abdominal aortic wall.
Selective congenital absence of teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited intestinal trehalase deficiency impairs carbohydrate digestion; gastrointestinal enzyme dysfunction defines the disease despite intermittent symptoms.
Inflammation is located in the conjunctiva; the umbrella includes infectious and noninfectious causes, so an infectious or immune mechanism is not universal.
